title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Linen Lake Postcard. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Linen Lake Postcard
options.thesis: The save-the-date is a Gun Lake postcard you can flip, not a wedding homepage.
options.viewport: One postcard fills the screen: lake face, James + Hannah as addressee, maroon JUL 4 2027 postmark, Bay Pointe Inn as caption; pointer tilts, click flips.
options.risk: Reads like a gift-shop souvenir if the type turns cute or the lake photo is generic stock.

raised.raise: Hall-scale object: the card is the entire first viewport, edge to edge, with no site chrome.
One-sheet evidence: linen grain, stamp bite, and handwriting stay visible as construction.
Fighting scale: the names and July 4, 2027 outrank the landscape caption.
Physical mark and snap: the date is the postmark; the flip carries inertia and settles like card stock.
Displacing fields: lake blue and maroon never mix; water owns the face, maroon owns stamp and verso ink.

options.label: Gun Lake Chart Plate
options.thesis: The announcement is a chart of Gun Lake, with the wedding as the marked sounding.
options.viewport: A full-bleed chart plate: James + Hannah in the title block, Bay Pointe Inn as a maroon X on the south shore, July 4 2027 in the neatline.
options.risk: This is the clever-coastal landing most lake weddings pick; familiar, and effective if you want that.

options.label: Fourth-of-July Star Atlas
options.thesis: July 4 over Gun Lake as a star atlas: James and Hannah are the constellation, the date is the ringed object.
options.viewport: A night plate fills the screen; the couple’s names label the figure; a maroon reticle locks JUL 4 2027; Bay Pointe Inn sits in the plate margin.
options.case: Holds identification: a Michigan lake night and fireworks sky is this audience’s real scene. Loses clarity: coordinates can bury the inn unless the date stays the ringed object.
options.risk: Reads as an astronomy app if the venue and date are not the object under the eye.

options.label: Indoor Weather Sun
options.lineage: monofrequency indoor sun in a mirrored hall
options.thesis: A maroon-dusk sun doubled in the lake, names as shore silhouettes.
options.viewport: One vast horizontal band; a half sun on the far shore completes itself in the water.
options.case: Loses both: guests do not identify with an art-hall sun, and a disc does not make the inn or the date unmistakable.
options.kept: Total environmental commitment — the object owns the whole viewport.
options.risk: Beautiful and mute: a guest cannot calendar a sun.

options.label: Orizuru Fold Sequence
options.lineage: thirty-two folds of a single uncut sheet into a crane
options.thesis: A maroon-and-blue square folded until the date stands as a crane.
options.viewport: A centered square and a numbered fold column; the finished bird holds July 4.
options.case: Loses both: folding hides the facts, and origami is not this family’s ritual.
options.kept: One continuous sheet with every prior crease still visible.
options.risk: Parents will not hunt a date through thirty-two steps.

options.label: Torn Flyer Wall
options.lineage: club walls of stapled photocopied flyers
options.thesis: Save-the-dates stapled over save-the-dates, torn back through earlier nights.
options.viewport: Heavy display caps at four scales; only the newest sheet fully legible.
options.case: Loses both: there is only one night, and a club wall is not an invitation parents will trust.
options.kept: Newest sheet fully legible at a scale that fights the frame.
options.risk: Reads as a basement show, not a lake wedding.

options.label: Cutting-Bench Rail
options.thesis: The weekend as frames on a perforated rail, July 4 flagged with tape.
options.viewport: A rail across the sheet; the flagged frame is the date; trims hang below.
options.case: Loses both: film-bench grammar is not a guest’s world, and a postmark is already a clearer physical mark.
options.kept: Inertial snap to a physical mark, never between frames.
options.risk: Looks like an editor’s tool wearing wedding copy.

options.label: Ebru Pigment Bath
options.lineage: floated pigment lifted onto paper in one contact
options.thesis: Light blue and maroon pigments combed on a bath, lifted once as the only copy.
options.viewport: A full-bleed bath; one lift reveals the names and date in the combed figure.
options.case: Loses both: marbling can swallow the date, and the craft is not West Michigan lake culture.
options.kept: Colors displace, never mix, at page scale.
options.risk: A guest remembers the swirl and forgets the inn.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Centered names, a coastal wash, Save the Date, the date, the inn — the page every wedding site ships.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional hero: names, date, Bay Pointe Inn, maybe a countdown.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from a coastal Canva template, by design.
